In Água Clara, Mato Grosso do Sul, the Military Police received an anonymous tip
that a man was selling drugs from a white VW Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras
neighbourhood on 4 November 2026. The driver fled when officers approached
but was caught after a chase of a few blocks. In all, five men were
arrested: four caught in flagrante for drug trafficking and association for
trafficking, and one taken on an outstanding arrest warrant. At the home of
the 30-year-old driver, officers found portions of marijuana and a precision
scale. The driver had been under investigation by the civil police's
General Investigations Section (SIG), whose work identified a second address
used to store a larger quantity of drugs.

At that address officers found 59 tablets of marijuana weighing about 54
kilograms and arrested two men, aged 18 and 20, at the scene. Two more
suspects were located at a snack bar by a joint Military and Civil Police task
force before the tablets were found. A third suspect, aged 22, was found
with about 500 grams of marijuana and a precision scale. In the car, police
found a portion of a cocaine-like substance, and at the suspect's home they
seized portions of marijuana, a precision scale, packaging materials and money.

Officers also recovered a bag of 19 portions of cocaine totalling about 120
grams, which police said the first suspect had discarded during the initial
stop. The operation ran from the night of Wednesday 4 November into
Thursday 5 November. Police reported seizing about 54.64 kilograms of drugs
in total, including marijuana and cocaine, along with a car, a motorcycle, three
precision scales, three mobile phones, packaging material and about 250 reais in
cash.

report.title: Truck driver remanded over hashish hidden in Ceuta port lorry
report.summary: A judge remanded a truck driver in custody on 15 November after UDYCO found bags of hashish hidden in a false bottom of his lorry at the port of Ceuta. Police gave no official weight; unofficial estimates ranged from more than 100 to fewer than 300 kilograms.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. On Sunday 15 November the driver was brought before a judicial authority, which ordered him remanded in custody (prisión preventiva) on suspicion of an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remains open amid suspicions of larger cargoes and heavy vehicles being concealed in spaces used as stash houses ('zulos') for storing hashish.

The women are suspected of planning to supply local agents, and police have registered a case and are investigating the wider interstate network.

report.body:
Police in Pudukkottai, Tamil Nadu, arrested two women suspected of smuggling
ganja by car from Andhra Pradesh. The two were identified as Vasanthi and
her niece Shanmugapriya, both from the Thiruvappur Kovilpatti area of
Pudukkottai.

Officers stopped a suspicious luxury car arriving from Andhra Pradesh toward
Pudukkottai at a vehicle check on Friday and found ganja packets stacked in
sacks in a concealed part of the car. Police seized about 26 kg of ganja
valued at roughly 13 lakh rupees and impounded the car used for the smuggling. The preliminary inquiry found that the pair planned to bring the ganja
sacks from Andhra Pradesh and distribute them to local agents in Pudukkottai and
its surrounding areas.

Police registered a case and are investigating who the key figures in the
interstate ganja network are and who drove the car. The arrest followed
stepped-up surveillance by Tamil Nadu police aimed at curbing drug circulation
in the state.

Three Thai nationals were arrested at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA)
in Katunayake on 15 October 2026 for allegedly trying to smuggle hashish worth
approximately Rs. 51 million into Sri Lanka. Police Narcotics Bureau (PNB)
officers made the arrests early on 15 October while the suspects were attempting
to leave the airport with the narcotics. The three suspects, aged 22, 22
and 33, were reportedly employed as drivers in Thailand.

They had arrived at Katunayake Airport from Bangkok, Thailand, aboard Thai
Airways flight TG-307 at approximately 12.30 a.m. on 15 October. During an
inspection of their three pieces of luggage, officers discovered 5.96 kilograms
of hashish, carefully concealed inside cosmetic product containers. The
three suspects, along with the seized narcotics, were scheduled to be produced
before the Negombo Magistrate’s Court on 15 October. The Police Narcotics
Bureau at Katunayake Airport was conducting further investigations.

the raid. The workers were busy sorting the marijuana buds to prepare them
for immediate customer delivery. The Myanmar workers were paid 200 to 300
baht a day to sort and pack the buds. Police suspect the Vietnamese man was
managing the daily operations like a corporate supervisor. Immigration

Police seized more than five tons of marijuana hidden in a luxury Bangkok rental
home. Black trash bags stuffed with cannabis buds were scattered across all
three floors of the home. The property was outfitted with a custom exhaust
pipe system to try and hide the heavy scent. Neighbors endured the heavy
scent for weeks before finally alerting the local authorities. The police
raid followed a year-long investigation after neighbours complained about a
strong cannabis smell emanating from the house.

Ms. Onanong Srisuwan, a legal officer from the Department of Thai Traditional
and Alternative Medicine, explained the violation. She said, processing and
selling cannabis requires a strict local permit. The operators held a
license that was valid only for Nong Bua Lamphu province, not Bangkok.
Offenders can face up to one year in prison or a fine of 20,000 baht.

plants and dangerous pesticides during a search warrant in Taft, California. He was Rogelio Lorenzo Francisca, 32, of Guerrero, Mexico, arrested on

delaying, resisting or obstructing an officer. He was booked into the Taft
jail facility.

the warrant on 8 October 2026, assisted by the sheriff's High Intensity Drug
Trafficking Areas task force (KC-HIDTA) and the Taft Police Department. The
warrant was in the 27000 block of Highway 119 in Taft. During the search, a
total of 660 marijuana plants were eradicated. Dangerous pesticides were
also found within the grow site.

The Sheriff's Office said the investigation was active and ongoing. Anyone
with information was asked to contact the Kern County Sheriff's Office or Kern
Secret Witness.
